A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ERGO research work. All 17 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, latency measurements, masking experiments, reward ablations, and qualitative results for ERGO.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, reward-design experiments, and latency comparisons in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Appendix A revises the written GRPO update trajectory: v1 appends only o_region to GroupRollouts, whereas v2 appends (o_region, o_acc). This is a limited algorithm-specification change; the two-stage pipeline, models, and reward equations remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation or training runs changed.

E1.justification: Table 2 adds model evaluations on TreeBench and VisualProbe at both pixel budgets, substantially expanding high-resolution VQA evaluation coverage. The original V*, HR-Bench, MME-RWLite, and conventional multimodal evaluations remain, as do the ArxivQA and V* training data.

E2.justification: MiniO3 is newly evaluated in Tables 2 and 3, and Table 2 adds Qwen2.5-VL controls at the constrained resolutions. Table 4 expands the former ERGO-versus-Qwen latency comparison to include DeepEyes and MiniO3. Appendix C further compares ERGO with TreeVGR, DeepEyes, and Mini-o3 under native and adjusted configurations.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluations varying maximum tool calls over 1, 2, and 4, plus native-configuration and latency-constrained comparisons that adjust pixel budgets or tool-call counts (Table 4 and Appendix C). Section 5.2 also corrects the coverage-score definition. The newly disclosed general four-call cap does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 6 adds broader reward-weight sensitivity tests, GLM4.5V-108B and InternVL3-78B reward-model variants, and linear versus step-function box rewards. New Figures 8–9 examine the alternative reward and resulting crop collapse. Tool-call and latency-budget sensitivity analyses also expand substantially; the original masking, region-size, and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting. Training rollouts are not repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds benchmark, comparator, latency, and ablation results while retaining shared per-benchmark Table 2 values and Table 5 results. New TreeBench results show ERGO below TreeVGR at the 1280 budget, 41.7 versus 48.2; the new linear box-reward variant scores 51.0 versus 58.4 for the step function. Reported averages such as ERGO's 69.3 in v1 versus 58.4 in v2 cover different benchmark sets and are not same-setting performance declines.

T1.justification: Section 5.2 corrects the Target Coverage Score definition. v1 uses a sum with an unused index and a maximum ranging over both predicted and ground-truth boxes; v2 explicitly averages each ground-truth box's best coverage over predicted boxes. This changes the written mathematical aggregation, although Figure 5 retains the same results. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain efficient coarse-to-fine reasoning, the TCE reward, and improved accuracy with fewer vision tokens. The abstract retains the same 4.7-point V* improvement, 23% token usage, and threefold speedup claim. The expanded experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of reward-weight balance and extends the robustness argument across reward-model families. It also explains that linear box rewards encourage excessive crop shrinking because shrinking is easier than improving region verification. Appendix C adds interpretations of efficiency under native and latency-constrained settings; the original main mechanism explanation remains.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents ERGO's single-tool-call design, the main evaluations' four-call cap, and pixel/tool budgets for the added latency comparisons. Retained qualitative examples gain explicit 1280×28×28 processing labels. Appendix B's training configuration is unchanged. The abstract now mentions code availability without explicitly mentioning models, but this does not establish that model access was withdrawn.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lai et al.'s Mini-o3 reference and incorporates it into the competitor discussion and evaluations. The substantive positioning against visual reasoning, token pruning, and efficiency-oriented RL in Section 6 remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. Changes include local wording corrections, explicitly naming DeepEyes, expanded experimental explanations, a new latency appendix, and an LLM usage disclosure. The qualitative appendix moves from C to D without replacing its examples.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICLR layout with different text widths, headers, typography, and figure placement. Figures 1–2 receive visual and caption edits; Tables 2, 3, 4, and 6 expand; and Figures 8–9 and Tables 8–9 are added. Existing qualitative figures are renumbered and annotated, while their underlying examples remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons against reasoning competitors under tool-call, native, and latency constraints strengthen the practical-efficiency evidence beyond v1's latency comparison with Qwen alone. Expanded reward ablations also probe useful failure modes. These gains are moderated by reporting inconsistencies: Table 2 retains an all-benchmarks superiority claim despite the new TreeBench counterexamples, and its reported averages do not match simple averages of the displayed scores without an explained alternative aggregation.
